'''Laurence Daniel Marks''' (born July 4, 1954) is an American physicist. He is a professor emeritus of [[materials science]] and engineering at [[Northwestern University]]. He has contributed to the study of [[nanoparticle]]s and worked in the fields of [[electron microscopy]], [[diffraction]], and [[crystallography]].

==Early life and education==
Marks attended [[Trinity School of John Whitgift]] in [[Croydon]], England. He played chess competitively for the school and won the [[British Chess Championship]] Under 21 in 1973.<ref>{{cite web |title=British Champions 1904 – present |url=http://www.englishchess.org.uk/british-champions-1904-present/ |publisher=The English Chess Federation |access-date=17 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180626111649/https://www.englishchess.org.uk/british-champions-1904-present/ |archive-date=26 June 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CBsuAQAAIAAJ&q=%22Laurence+D.+Marks%22+-wikipedia |title=The British Chess Magazine |date=1966 |publisher=Trubner & Company |volume=86 |page=45 |language=en |via=Google Books}}</ref>

Marks graduated from [[King's College, Cambridge]], with a [[B.A.]] in chemistry in 1976.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=L. D. Marks |url=https://appliedphysics.northwestern.edu/people/faculty/l-d-marks.html |access-date=2023-11-11 |website=Applied Physics Graduate Program - Northwestern University |language=en}}</ref> From 1976 to 1980, he was a research student at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at Cambridge, where he worked with [[Archibald Howie]] on electron microscopy and the structure of metal crystals.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Marks |first1=L. D. |last2=Howie |first2=A. |date=1979 |title=Multiply-twinned particles in silver catalysts |url=http://www.numis.northwestern.edu/Research/Articles/1979-81/79_MTP.pdf |journal=Nature |volume=282 |issue=5735 |page=196 |bibcode=1979Natur.282..196M |doi=10.1038/282196a0 |s2cid=4256301}}</ref><ref name="MarksCV" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |date=Summer 2015 |title=What's On the Cover |url=https://www.amercrystalassn.org/assets/RefleXions/SUMMER2015RS.pdf |journal=ACA RefleXions: American Crystallographic Association Matters |issue=2 |page=17}}</ref> He received his [[Ph.D.]] in physics from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1980.<ref name=":0" /> His dissertation was titled, ''The Structure of Small Silver Particles''.<ref name=MarksCV>{{cite web |title=Curriculum vitae — Laurence Daniel Marks |url=http://www.mccormick.northwestern.edu/docs/public_cv/Marks-Laurence-CV.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201023115317/https://www.mccormick.northwestern.edu/docs/public_cv/Marks-Laurence-CV.pdf |archive-date=23 October 2020 |access-date=10 November 2023 |publisher=Northwestern University}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Marks |first=Laurence Daniel |date=1980 |title=The structure of small silver particles |url=https://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/permalink/f/iojq9k/44CAM_ALMA21429717800003606 | type=PhD thesis |publisher=University of Cambridge}}  ([http://www.numis.northwestern.edu/thesis/LDM_Thesis.pdf Full text])</ref>

==Career==
From 1980 to 1983, Marks was a post-doctoral research assistant at the Cavendish Laboratory.<ref name="MarksCV" /> From 1983 to 1985, he was a post-doctoral research assistant with the Department of Physics at [[Arizona State University]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]].<ref name="MarksCV" /> [[File:Marks_Decahedron,_stable_shape_for_five-fold_twinned_nanoparticles.gif|thumb|Marks Decahedron|left]]In March 1985, Marks joined the faculty of [[Northwestern University]] as an [[assistant professor]] in the Department of Materials Science & Engineering.<ref name="MarksCV" /> He received a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] for physics in 1987.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=1987-04-19 |title=Sloan Foundation Awards 90 Grants |language=en-US |pages=1.42 |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/04/19/nyregion/sloan-foundation-awards-90-grants.html |access-date=2023-11-12 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

Marks was promoted to [[professor]] in June 1992.<ref name="MarksCV" /> He was chair of the [[IUCr]] Commission on Electron Crystallography for two terms from 2005 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=IUCr |date=2009-09-01 |title=International Union of Crystallography Twenty-First General Assembly and International Congress of Crystallography, Osaka, Japan, 23–31 August 2008 |url=http://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/2009/05/00/es0367/es0367bdy.html#SECA4.10 |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section A: Foundations of Crystallography |language=en |volume=65 |issue=5 |pages=390–442 |doi=10.1107/S0108767308033643 |issn=0108-7673|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=IUCr |date=2012-09-01 |title=Twenty-Second General Assembly and International Congress of Crystallography, Madrid, Spain, 22–30 August 2011 |url=http://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/2012/05/00/es0389/es0389bdy.html#SECA5.11 |journal=Acta Crystallographica Section A: Foundations of Crystallography |language=en |volume=68 |issue=5 |pages=607–664 |doi=10.1107/S010876731200414X |issn=0108-7673|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 2019, he was a senior visiting scientist with the Suzhou Institute of Nano-tech and Nano-bionics (SINANO) of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":2" /> In July 2023, Marks was selected for a  [[Fulbright Scholar|Fulbright U.S. Scholar Program]] that allowed him to study [[Triboelectricity|triboelecticity]] in Australia.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Fellman |first=Megan |date=July 27, 2023 |title=Laurence Marks Receives Fulbright Award |url=https://www.mccormick.northwestern.edu/news/articles/2023/07/laurence-marks-receives-fulbright-award/ |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Northwestern McCormick School of Engineering |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Laurence Marks |url=https://fulbrightscholars.org/grantee/laurence-marks |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Fulbright Scholar Program}}</ref> As of September 2023, Marks is an [[emeritus]] professor at Northwestern University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Commencement Program |url=https://www.northwestern.edu/graduation/images/2023commencementprogram.pdf |website=Northwestern University}}</ref>

Starting from his PhD work, he studied [[Crystal twinning|nanotwinning]], leading toward a way to directly image the atomic scale of nano-surfaces.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2019 |title=Professor Laurence Marks from Northwestern University of USA Visits SINANO |url=http://english.sinano.cas.cn/ns/es/201908/t20190802_213891.html |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Suzhou Institute of Nano-Tech and Nano-Bionics, Chinese Academy of Sciences}}</ref> One of his early research efforts led to the discovery of a type of [[nanoparticle]] now known as the [[Marks decahedron]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> He has been actively involved in many aspects of [[electron microscope]] development,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jacoby |first=Mitch |date=2008-06-23 |title=Electron Microscopy For Chemists |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/86/i25/Electron-Microscopy-Chemists.html |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=[[Chemical & Engineering News]] |language=en}}</ref> including new methods to solve [[surface]] structures<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Diebold |first=Ulrike |author-link=Ulrike Diebold |date=March 2010 |title=Surface science goes inorganic |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat2708 |journal=[[Nature Materials]] |language=en |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=185–187 |doi=10.1038/nmat2708 |pmid=20168340 |bibcode=2010NatMa...9..185D |issn=1476-4660|url-access=subscription }}</ref> as well as using these instruments to discover phenomena such as graphitic materials on [[hip implant]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Drahl |first=Carmen |date=2012-01-02 |title=Carbon Layer Lubricates All-Metal Hips |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/90/i1/Carbon-Layer-LubricatesMetal-Hips.html |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=[[Chemical & Engineering News]] |language=en}}</ref> He also studies how [[static electricity]] is generated by rubbing, a phenomenon known as the [[triboelectric effect]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2019/09/solving-the-longstanding-mystery-of-how-friction-leads-to-static-electricity|title=Solving the longstanding mystery of how friction leads to static electricity|website=news.northwestern.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fox |first=Alen |date=2019-09-12 |title=The secret of static electricity? It's shocking |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/secret-static-electricity-it-s-shocking |access-date=2025-09-22 |website=[[Science Magazine]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.discovermagazine.com/static-electricity-shapes-everyday-life-but-its-origin-remains-shockingly-mysterious-48645|title=Static Electricity Shapes Everyday Life — but Its Origin Remains Shockingly Mysterious|first=Max|last=Bennett|date=February 5, 2026|website=Discover Magazine}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 1989, Marks received the Burton Award from the [[Microscopy Society of America]] for achievements in the fields of microscopy and microanalysis by a scientist under 40 years of age.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Society Awards Recipients By Year |url=https://microscopy.org/msa-society-awards-recipients |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Microscopy Society of America |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> He received the Bertram E. Warren Award from the [[American Crystallographic Association]] in 2015<ref>{{cite web |title=2015 Award Winners |url=http://www.amercrystalassn.org/2015-awardees |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170611063334/http://www.amercrystalassn.org/2015-awardees |archive-date=11 June 2017 |access-date=15 August 2015 |website=American Crystallographic Association |publisher=Internet Archive}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> and the International Conference on the Structure of Surfaces Prize in 2017.<ref name="ICSOS">{{cite web |title=ICSOS Prize winners |url=http://www3.lut.fi/projectsites/icsos/prize.html |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=International Conference on the Structure of Surfaces (ICSOS)}}</ref>

Marks was elected as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2001, for his "contributions to quantitative imaging and diffraction methods for determining the atomic structure of surfaces and bulk materials",<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive (M) |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=M&year=2014&unit_id=&institution= |publisher=American Physical Society |access-date=15 August 2015}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[Microscopy Society of America]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MSA Fellows |url=https://microscopy.org/MSA-Fellows |access-date=2023-10-14 |website=Microscopy Society of America}}</ref>
